blocks.text: Under Sampling, Over Sampling, SMOTE, and ADASYN all genuinely shared one thing in common, every single one of them changes the actual training data itself, removing rows, duplicating them, or generating new synthetic ones. Class weighting breaks from that entire family, leaving the training data completely, genuinely untouched, and instead changing how the learning algorithm itself penalizes mistakes.

This topic covers exactly how a weighted loss function makes misclassifying the minority class genuinely more costly during training, the standard formula behind automatic balanced weighting, how to apply this directly through a single parameter in many scikit-learn models, the option to specify fully custom weights for finer control, and a real, genuine limitation, this technique only works for models that actually support a weighted loss function in the first place.
1. The Real Advantage: The Data Stays Untouched

blocks.alt: Class weighting leaves the original data unchanged

blocks.text: Every genuine original row stays exactly as it was, nothing gets removed, exactly the real cost under sampling carried, and nothing gets duplicated or synthetically generated, exactly the real costs over sampling, SMOTE, and ADASYN each carried in their own way. Class weighting genuinely sidesteps every single one of those specific risks at once, simply by never touching the data at all.

This is a genuinely real, meaningful advantage worth appreciating directly, every technique covered so far in this module involved some real tradeoff baked into the data itself, class weighting moves that entire tradeoff somewhere else instead, into how the algorithm actually learns from data left fully intact.
2. How a Weighted Loss Function Actually Works

blocks.alt: Minority class error gets weighted more heavily

blocks.text: During training, a model genuinely computes a loss value reflecting how wrong its predictions are, and adjusts itself to reduce that loss over time. Class weighting multiplies the loss contribution of each individual training example by a genuine weight tied to its class, so a mistake on a minority example genuinely counts for more, and a mistake on a majority example genuinely counts for less, than it otherwise would.

This directly changes the algorithm real incentive during training, without needing a single extra or removed row, a model genuinely learns to care more about getting minority predictions right, simply because doing so now carries a genuinely larger reward, and getting them wrong carries a genuinely larger real penalty.
3. The Standard Balanced Weighting Formula

blocks.alt: Class size feeds an inverse proportion into a balanced weight

blocks.text: A genuine, standard formula sets each class weight inversely proportional to its own frequency, a class making up only 5 percent of the data genuinely receives a considerably higher weight than a class making up 95 percent. This directly mirrors the real intuition behind this entire technique, a genuinely rarer class needs a genuinely stronger incentive for the model to pay proper attention to it.

This formula is genuinely standard enough that it rarely needs to be computed by hand, as the next section covers directly, most machine learning libraries genuinely compute it automatically with a single parameter setting.
4. A Worked Example
Applying class_weight equals balanced directly in scikit-learn LogisticRegression shows how simply this technique can be applied, with no changes to the training data whatsoever.

code.content:
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
import pandas as pd

X = pd.DataFrame({"amount": [50, 60, 45, 5000, 30, 70, 40, 6200]})
y = pd.Series([0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1])

model = LogisticRegression(class_weight="balanced")
model.fit(X, y)

print("Classes:", model.classes_)

blocks.text: The exact same 8 original rows, 6 majority and 2 minority, went directly into training here, genuinely unchanged, with the balanced weighting handled entirely internally by the model itself during its actual loss computation.

blocks.text: 5. Class Weight Balanced in scikit-learn

blocks.alt: A scikit-learn model can be set with class_weight equals balanced

blocks.text: Many scikit-learn models genuinely support a class_weight parameter directly, LogisticRegression, SVC, DecisionTreeClassifier, and RandomForestClassifier among them. Setting it to balanced genuinely computes the inverse frequency weighting formula covered above automatically, requiring no manual calculation at all.

This genuine, single parameter setting is often the very first, simplest thing worth trying on an imbalanced classification problem, before reaching for any of the more involved data level techniques covered earlier in this module.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Try class_weight equals balanced as a genuinely quick first step on an imbalanced problem, before reaching for the more involved data level techniques covered earlier in this module. It costs one parameter and no data changes at all.

blocks.text: 6. Custom Weights for Finer Control

blocks.alt: Default balanced weights can be replaced with custom weights

blocks.text: Beyond the automatic balanced default, class_weight also genuinely accepts a manual dictionary mapping each class to its own specific weight, offering genuinely finer control than the standard inverse frequency formula provides. This matters in real cases where the genuine, real world cost of a false negative and a false positive are not symmetric, missing a genuine fraud case might be considerably more costly than a false alarm, a distinction the automatic balanced formula alone cannot capture.

This flexibility connects directly to real, practical business considerations, the right weight is not always just about class frequency, it can genuinely reflect the real, differing costs of different kinds of mistakes for a specific, real problem.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Custom class weights genuinely let real, differing business costs shape training directly, not just raw class frequency. A false negative on a fraud case can genuinely be weighted far more heavily than a false positive, if that reflects real, practical cost.

blocks.text: 7. A Real, Genuine Limitation: Model Support

blocks.alt: Some models support class weighting directly while others do not

blocks.text: Class weighting genuinely only works for models that actually have a weighted loss function to adjust in the first place, logistic regression, support vector machines, and tree based models all genuinely qualify. A plain K-nearest neighbors model, by contrast, genuinely has no loss function being minimized during training at all, it simply looks up nearby points directly, so class weighting genuinely does not apply to it in the same direct way.

This is a genuinely real, practical contrast with every data level technique covered earlier in this module, under sampling, over sampling, SMOTE, and ADASYN all genuinely work with any model at all, since they change the data itself rather than depending on a specific algorithm internal mechanism, while class weighting genuinely requires that specific mechanism to exist.

blocks.text: 8. Class Weighting Versus What Comes Next

blocks.alt: Class weighting is covered here, threshold tuning comes next

blocks.text: Class weighting offers a genuinely clean, data preserving alternative to every technique covered earlier in this module, at the real cost of requiring specific model support. One final, even simpler option remains, one that touches neither the data nor the algorithm training process at all.

Threshold Tuning, the final topic in this module, adjusts only how a model already trained predictions get converted into a final class decision, a genuinely different, prediction time fix that works alongside any of the techniques covered throughout this entire module.

The standard balanced formula sets weights genuinely inversely proportional to class frequency.
